clue.text: Deprived fellow wearing hat

indicators.note: whatever is wearing a hat has it on top and around it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A man down on his luck with nothing left but a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The fellow goes inside the beret, between its E and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means robbed or left without something, a close synonym of deprived.

clue.text: Graduate having quiet party

parts.note: Bachelor of Arts, a graduate's degree

explanation.surface: A new graduate throws a low-key celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A bash is informal slang for a party or celebration.

clue.text: Put down regarding journalists

parts.note: the press is the body of journalists

explanation.surface: Something about reporters being suppressed or silenced.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress a revolt is to subdue or crush it, which is what putting it down means.

clue.text: Brief, short affair includes upstanding support

indicators.note: one word includes another by holding it within its own letters
in a down entry, standing up means reading from the bottom upward, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: the peg that supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A short-lived fling that nonetheless involves some upright support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief, short affair' reads as one description, but the comma splits off the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleeting means passing quickly and lasting only a short time, as anything brief does.

clue.text: Male is leading bad behaviour

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
chief as an adjective means principal or leading

explanation.surface: A man is the ringleader in some misconduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief is playful or troublesome misconduct, the naughtiness of children especially.

clue.text: Poison from popular religious faction — one police investigate finally

parts.note: the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it

explanation.surface: Detectives look into a poisoning linked to a popular cult.
explanation.definitionFit: An insecticide is a chemical poison used for killing insects.

clue.text: Charlie punches holding instruments

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to lamp someone is British slang for hitting them

explanation.surface: Charlie throws punches at some tools in a workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punches' looks like tools of its own, but it is a verb: lamp is British slang for hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamps are tools that grip and hold objects firmly in place.

clue.text: Foolish jerk follows papers on moon

indicators.note: follows says that piece comes after the ones named next, at the end of the entry

parts.note: Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: Some idiot reacts to newspaper stories about the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'papers on moon' puts the papers above the moon; the twitch comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means very stupid, a synonym of foolish.

clue.text: My fan mail redirected to patriarch perhaps

indicators.note: post that is redirected goes somewhere new, just as these letters are sent into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity's admirer post is forwarded to the head of the household.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarch heads a household, and a man devoted to wife and children is one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Great to eat quiet meal

indicators.note: what eats something takes it inside itself

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: How lovely to have a peaceful dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening meal, often a light one.

clue.text: Part of Shane's cap is manufacturer's fantasy

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: Someone called Shane owns a cap that turns out to be the maker's fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapism is retreat into daydreams and fantasy to avoid reality.

clue.text: Investment in Peruvian cattle development

indicators.note: development changes something into a new form, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone puts money into a South American livestock scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Venture capital is money invested in new or growing businesses in return for a stake.

clue.text: Train heroic Byzantine speaker

indicators.note: byzantine means intricate and convoluted, so the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Coaching a heroic orator from Constantinople.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; Byzantine does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhetorician is an expert in the art of persuasive public speaking.

clue.text: Hinted Iris could be cut off

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent suggests that Iris may lose her inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cut off is to be denied an inheritance by one's family.

clue.text: Detectives drink strange tea and scatter

indicators.note: strange letters are out of their normal order

explanation.surface: Police officers sip some odd tea and then disperse.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissipate is to disperse or scatter, as a crowd or mist does.

clue.text: Froth starts to spill copiously upsetting mum

indicators.note: the starts of the following words means their opening letters

parts.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A frothing pan boils over everywhere, annoying Mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' suggests reversing a word, but here it only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is the layer of froth or film that rises to the surface of a liquid.

clue.text: Arsenal publication

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a store for weapons and ammunition
second meaning: a periodical with articles and pictures

explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal looks like the London football club, so this reads as a club's programme; it is a weapons store.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an ammunition store and a regularly issued periodical.

clue.text: Obnoxious person with a drink

parts.note: sod is British slang for an unpleasant person

explanation.surface: An unpleasant character holding a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is fizzy water or a carbonated soft drink.

clue.text: Last month grass gets laid down

parts.note: DEC is the abbreviation for December, the last month of the year

explanation.surface: In December some turf was put down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid down' looks like turf being laid, but it means a rule being set.
explanation.definitionFit: Decreed means ordained by authority, as when a law is laid down.

clue.text: Reason proposal includes one tank

indicators.note: one word includes others by holding them within its own letters

parts.note: a formal proposal in a debate

explanation.surface: A motion is tabled to buy a single tank, for some reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Motivation is the reason behind someone's actions or behaviour.

clue.text: Loutish setter will be around right before date

indicators.note: before places the remaining piece after everything already built

parts.note: the setter is I, and I will contracts to I'll

indicators.note: around says the word goes about another, holding it inside

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: The setter promises to stay put until the appointment, despite being boorish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-bred means badly brought up, rude and uncouth, much like loutish.

clue.text: Colour of home before excavation over

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of what follows

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: The shade of a house before the digging is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like it means finished, but it is just its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet colour, one of the rainbow's seven.

clue.text: Prepared sociable dinner of no great size

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready from raw materials, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone cooked a friendly meal, but not a very big one.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsiderable means small or insignificant in amount or size.

clue.text: Unemployed individual demanding legitimate employment primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letters are taken

parts.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A jobless person insisting on finding honest work.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means not working or out of work, so unemployed.

clue.text: Healthy rage secretary turned around getting drink

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: An angry, healthy secretary spins round and gets a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Draw wine arranged in rows

parts.note: a drawn game is a tie

explanation.surface: Sketching wine bottles lined up on shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like sketching, but it is a game ending level.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiered means arranged in layered rows, one above another, like stadium seating.

clue.text: Last nurse embracing love completely

parts.note: the end is the last part

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap one's arms around, so one piece holds another

parts.note: to tend is to look after
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A final nurse hugging someone with complete affection.
explanation.definitionFit: End-to-end means from one end to the other, thoroughly and completely.

clue.text: Sell bike part on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound

explanation.surface: Someone advertises a bicycle component over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To peddle is to sell goods, typically by going from place to place.
